name: DM Champ
what: An AI sales agent that chats with leads and books calls. Agencies (companies that do marketing for clients) can put their own brand on it (white-label it) and resell it.
title: DM Champ sat near $10K a month for a year, then hit $28K after it changed who it sells to
dek: It started by waking up one clinic's old leads on WhatsApp, found customers through cold email, AppSumo (a site that sells lifetime deals on software) and a webinar (a live online talk), and then turned itself into a tool agencies resell. Its MRR (monthly recurring revenue: what subscribers pay every month) is $135,927 today. That is far above any month's revenue so far, and we couldn't find out why.
pattern: Start with a problem you saw at work

first_revenue.text: A clinic found through cold email paid about €2,000 a month after DM Champ messaged its old leads on WhatsApp.
first_revenue.label: Claimed

first_customers.text: Cold email brought the first customers. Later channels were AppSumo and affiliates (people paid a cut of each sale they bring in).
first_customers.label: Claimed

phases.name: The problem at work
phases.story: The founder ran a marketing agency and did the marketing for a hair transplant clinic. He saw clinics losing leads because nobody answered WhatsApp, Instagram and website chats fast enough. That became the idea.

number.v: Company founded Nov 7 2022 (AppSumo) or Jan 2023 (Starter Story)
number.label: Sources differ

phases.lesson: The best ideas often come from a problem you watch people have every day.

phases.name: Wake up old leads
phases.story: The founder cold-emailed local clinics (emailed businesses that didn't know him yet) using a tool called Instantly. Three were interested and he followed up with one. That clinic had fewer than 200 old leads; the AI messaged them on WhatsApp and the clinic started paying every month. The product was first called Whatz.ai, and in 2024 the homepage still sold exactly this.

number.v: €2,000 a month from the first clinic
number.label: Claimed

phases.lesson: Start with a result a business can see in money, like customers who come back.

phases.name: A cheap launch with lots of refunds
phases.story: DM Champ went on AppSumo. It made about €20,000 from 300 customers, but 40% asked for refunds. The founder blames the cheapest tier, which 'attracted tire-kickers' (people who look but never really buy).
phases.lesson: Price too low and you attract people who were never going to use it.

phases.name: One webinar, and ads that backfired
phases.story: A business coach the team knew ran a 60-minute webinar for 300 people. The founder says 'we had $20K in Stripe' two minutes after the offer went live, from 80 customers. Meta ads (Facebook and Instagram ads) closed 15% of leads, but those customers cancelled after three months.
phases.lesson: Someone else's audience that already trusts them can sell more in an hour than months of ads.

phases.name: Stuck around $10K
phases.story: In mid-2025 the homepage dared visitors: 'Find Us an AI Sales Agent More Human than Ours and We'll Send You $100'. In March 2026 the founder told Starter Story the business made about $10,000 a month. Stripe agrees: monthly revenue stayed between $6,241 and $12,263 from December 2025 to September 2026.
phases.lesson: A clever headline gets attention, but it doesn't change who your customer is.

phases.name: Sell to agencies instead
phases.story: By July 2026 the homepage spoke to agencies: put your own logo on the AI and resell it to your clients. The founder calls the 2026 AppSumo launch its third, and says 'What we used to make in a year, we now make in a month.' Stripe revenue nearly tripled in October 2026.
phases.lesson: Sometimes the fix is a new buyer, not a new feature: sell to the people who sell to everyone else.

fact_checks.claim: The business makes about $10,000 a month
fact_checks.found: True when it was said: TrustMRR shows $10,310 in March 2026. But October 2026 was $28,426, and MRR on Nov 18 2026 is $135,927, far above any single month's revenue so far. We couldn't verify why MRR is so much higher.
fact_checks.label: Verified

fact_checks.found: TrustMRR shows $244,756 all-time in the Stripe account it reads. AppSumo's sales numbers aren't public, so we can't check this.
fact_checks.label: Couldn't verify

fact_checks.found: AppSumo says founded Nov 7 2022. Starter Story says January 2023.
fact_checks.label: Sources differ

checklist: Write down one problem you saw a business near you struggle with this month (slow replies, missed calls, no-shows).
Offer to fix it for one business by hand first, before you build anything.
Send ten short, personal emails to local businesses with that offer and follow up with anyone who replies.
Pick a result you can show in money, like old customers who came back, and measure it.
If you sell a cheap version, ask whether the cheapest buyers will actually use it before you set the price.
Find one person with an audience that trusts them and ask if they'd share your thing for a cut of each sale.
